subject: Service stability impacts renewal — discussion about premium options and commitments
messages:
From: Raj Kumar <raj@acmedata.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: Michelle Torres <m.torres@acmedata.com>, procurement@acmedata.com
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency — impact to evaluation & renewal timeline

Hi Tessa,

Wanted to loop back quickly — over the last three weeks we've seen repeated latency spikes during peak ingest windows. The engineering team attached a zip of traces and a short runbook of what we observed. These blips are affecting two of our customer-facing features (search and recommendations), which in turn is making leadership nervous about moving to a larger committed tier as we enter renewal later this quarter.

Short questions: can Redwood commit to a P50/P90 latency target for our workload if we upgrade to premium (SLA-backed) capacity? If so, what would the timeline look like to get a pilot running? We need concrete SLAs and an escalation path documented for the execs.

Attachments: acme_latency_snaps-202611.zip (logs/trace excerpts)

Thanks,
Raj
Sr. Engineering Manager
Acme Data Systems
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Raj Kumar <raj@acmedata.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-02T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency — impact to evaluation & renewal timeline

Raj — thanks for the detail and the logs. I reviewed them with our reliability team (cc). Short answer: yes, we can offer a pilot on our Dedicated Premium path with SLA commitments scoped to your workload, but there are trade-offs to define up-front (burst capacity, KV cache sizing, and warm-POPs).

Next steps I propose:
- Internal health review: Redwood will run a focused analysis on the attached traces and reply with a short mitigation plan by 2026-12-04.
- Pilot design: if the plan looks good, we can stand up a 2-week dedicated pilot in the us-west region to validate P50/P90 numbers. Estimated lead time for capacity allocation is ~10 business days after SOW sign.
- Executive note: I'll draft a short one-pager for your execs that lays out the SLA, escalation playbook, and rollback criteria.

I'll attach a pricing sketch and a temporary SOW for review. Can you confirm the renewal window you mentioned so we can align timings?

—Tessa
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-03T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Production latency — impact to evaluation & renewal timeline

Internal — quick notes after looking at the traces:
- Spikes align with their daily bulk imports (09:00-10:30 PST). Likely K/V cache miss storms + long-tail tokenization from larger batch requests.
- Short-term mitigations: prefix caching on the ingest path, tune batching window to 15ms, and reserve a small reserved pool to absorb headroom.
- For an SLA we need to scope the sequence-length distribution and a sample qps curve — we should ask Acme for a 48-hour pcap or telemetry dump, not just logs.

I'll draft pilot config and a resource delta estimate. Grace — can you prepare a conservative P50/P90 estimate for the proposed reserved pool?

Sergio
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Raj Kumar <raj@acmedata.com>, Michelle Torres <m.torres@acmedata.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, procurement@acmedata.com
Date: 2026-12-09T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: Pilot proposal & premium pricing sketch for SLA-backed renewal path

Raj / Michelle — thanks again for the patience. Attached is a short pilot proposal and a pricing sketch for the Premium Dedicated path. Highlights:
- 14-day dedicated pilot in us-west with a capped reserved pool (config attached).
- P50 target: < 60ms for generation requests at your reported median size; P90 target: < 220ms for peak windows given the reserved pool described.
- Escalation path: 15-minute on-call response, 2-hour mitigation SLA, and credits if we miss SLA per the proposed SLO table.
- Estimated timeline from SOW signature to pilot start: 10 business days.

We attached SOW draft (SOW-draft-acme-20261214.docx) and the premium pricing PDF. If you want a shortened exec summary I can prepare one for your leadership.

Would you be available to take the pilot decision this Thursday (2026-12-16)? If so, procurement can sign the SOW and we can schedule capacity.

Attachments: premium-pricing-proposal-20261209.pdf, SOW-draft-acme-20261214.docx

Best,
Tessa
From: Raj Kumar <raj@acmedata.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Michelle Torres <m.torres@acmedata.com>, procurement@acmedata.com
Date: 2026-12-15T16:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot proposal & premium pricing sketch for SLA-backed renewal path

Tessa — appreciate the fast turnaround and the clarity on the escalation path. The execs asked two clarifying questions before we commit: 1) can Redwood guarantee region-failover behavior if us-west becomes degraded during pilot (we want an automatic fallback to us-east without manual reconfiguration), and 2) can you commit to an onboarding cutover window (max 4 hours) when we move to the reserved pool in production?

If you can confirm both items in writing, procurement will push the SOW to be signed this week. Otherwise we may ask for a short trial extension or a modest pricing credit tied to the cutover window.

Thanks — we'll aim to decide by end of week.

Raj
